title: restocking the empty shelf enables its button, and nothing else moves
question: does a write through the admin API reach the page a customer sees?
rule: catalog.setStock writes p.stock; web/app.js reads it on the next load and drops `disabled`.
`bb dotty during --reload` takes a frame each side of the command and reports the difference
as a MULTISET, so one button out of ten changing state is visible rather than averaged away.
The diff names the product because each button carries its own aria-label; without that
every row would read `Add to cart` and the multiset diff could not say WHICH one moved.

steps.name: a browser is listening, or nothing below this is about the product
empty the hub, so this scenario is about the screen and not about what ran before it
restocking it enables exactly one button and changes nothing else
steps.run: bb dotty during restock --reload --url {{base}}/ --json -- curl -s -o /dev/null -X POST {{base}}/admin/stock/p6 -H 'authorization: Bearer {{ops}}' -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"stock":9}'

steps.name: and that button is no longer disabled
put the shelf back, so the next run starts where this one did
